MUQATIL:23:101-105/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:23:101-105/r2.claim: Heavy scales are those of believers weighed down by righteous deeds; they are the successful.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p416#2/r1.claim: Those whose scales are heavy are the blessed people of Paradise.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p48#3/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p48#3/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p48#3/r1.claim: Asked whether people will remember their families at the Resurrection, the Prophet says not during three stations: the scale, distribution of records, and the bridge.

ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p48#3/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p48#3/r2.speaker: وهب بن منبه
ABDURRAZZAQ:v3p48#3/r2.claim: Wahb says that only the final outcomes of deeds are weighed.

THALABI:v7p57/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v7p57/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v7p57/r3.claim: Those whose scales are heavy succeed, while those whose scales are light lose themselves and remain in Hell.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v16p70/r1.claim: The author refers readers to his earlier explanation of these scales and the following verse in his commentary on al-Aʿraf.

JISHUMI:v7p5094/r8.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r8.speaker: حمزة، الكسائي
JISHUMI:v7p5094/r8.claim: Hamza and al-Kisa'i read شقاوتنا with an alif and open shin; others omit alif and use kasra. They are dialect variants, or respectively a verbal noun and noun according to Abu Muslim.

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p429#2/r1.claim: Those whose scales weigh heavily are successful.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
KASHSHAF-FULL:v3p206#2/r1.claim: Ibn Abbas explains the scales as weights of deeds, especially good deeds valued by God, citing 18:105.

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v4p156/r4.claim: Heavy scales mean good deeds outweighing; weight and lightness apply to forms God creates to embody deeds, according to reports.

TABRISI:23:101-108/r9.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:23:101-108/r9.speaker: author
TABRISI:23:101-108/r9.claim: Those whose scales are heavy through acts of obedience are the successful ones who are saved.

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r2.claim: After the Trumpet comes accounting and the division between the blessed, whose scales are heavy, and the wretched, whose scales are light.

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r3.claim: Some infer that everyone must belong either to the saved or the damned, ruling out people with no entitlement to reward or punishment and those whose two are equal.

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r4.claim: One interpretation treats the scales as a metaphor for justice.

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r5.claim: A second takes the scales as good deeds: deeds with value win, while weightless deeds like a mirage leave their doer in Hell.

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r6.claim: Ibn Abbas says the scales are plural of weighed things: righteous deeds valued by God; “no weight” means no worth.

RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v23p107/r7.claim: A third interpretation is a real scale with a tongue and two pans, weighing good deeds in beautiful form and evil deeds in ugly form.

BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r4.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r4.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:23:101-102/r4.claim: Heavy scales mean sound beliefs and good deeds that have weight and value before God; their possessors attain salvation and high degrees.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#2/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#2/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p131#2/r1.claim: “Scales” means the weighty good deeds, which have value with God, as in the statement that He will assign them no weight.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r1.claim: A person whose good deeds outweigh bad deeds by even one is among those with heavy scales.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r2.claim: The successful are those saved from Hell and admitted to Paradise.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r3.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās describes the successful as obtaining what they sought and escaping what they feared.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r5.speaker: أنس بن مالك
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p496#2/r5.claim: A report says an angel calls out the eternal felicity or misery of each person according to the balance's weight; Ibn Kathīr grades its chain weak because Dāwūd al-Muḥabbar is abandoned.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r4.claim: Successful people are weighed by accepted deeds; each deed may have its own appropriate scale, and the plural underscores God's power and the scope of weighing.

BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v5p222/r5.claim: The plural demonstrative may signal the many saved people or the universal weighing of every individual after the prior singular expressed the multiplicity of deeds.

BURSEVI:v6p76#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p76#2/r1.speaker: التأويلات النجمية
BURSEVI:v6p76#2/r1.claim: In an inward reading, divine care breathed into the heart raises its spiritual resurrection: worldly ties fall away as each person seeks God, absorbed in love and unconcerned with family, companions, or homeland.

BURSEVI:v6p76#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p76#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p76#2/r2.claim: The weighed things are sound beliefs and righteous deeds, which have worth and weight with God.

BURSEVI:v6p77/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v6p77/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v6p77/r1.claim: The successful attain every desired thing and escape every feared thing; the wording shifts from singular by grammatical form to plural by meaning.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#2/r1.claim: Heavy scales may mean measured good deeds—beliefs and actions—or plural balances weighed down by good deeds.

ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v18p66#2/r2.claim: The successful attain every desired thing and escape what they fear.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p124/r5.claim: The main consequence concerns the weighed deeds, answering the rejected plea for return; the denial of kinship first cuts off hope of help or intercession.

IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v18p126/r5.claim: Mentioning heavy scales praises believers and threatens polytheists, who have no good deeds on their scales; 25:23 is cited and 7:8 is discussed earlier.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p237/r8.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p237/r8.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-5-english:p237/r8.claim: Only people with heavy scales will succeed; God's servants who invite the rejecters to religion will triumph despite being mocked.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r1.claim: Salvation depends on the amount of reward earned through faith and good works: those whose deeds weigh heavily succeed, while those whose scales are light suffer loss and enter enduring Hell.

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r2.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r2.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:23:102/r2.claim: The nature of grave life, barzakh, resurrection, and the scales lies beyond empirical and rational knowledge; believers should affirm them and prepare for the afterlife.

STUDYQURAN:23:102/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:102/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:102/r1.claim: The commentary directs readers to its discussion of the scales of deeds at 101:6–9.

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r7.claim: The opposition of affluent and powerful people to prophets recurs throughout this surah, as elsewhere in the Quran.

STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:23:intro/r9.claim: The conclusion warns that disbelievers facing their perdition will wish to return to do good instead of evil, but it will be too late.
